name: Streaming ASR quality is materially worse than offline ASR
symptom: Streaming ASR systems (whisper-streaming, WhisperLive, etc.) produce transcription quality that is noticeably worse than offline Whisper on the same audio. Word error rates are higher, especially at segment boundaries.
root_cause: Streaming ASR must emit tokens with bounded latency as audio arrives, which requires chunked inference with causal masking and finite look-ahead. The model cannot see future audio context, so it makes decisions with incomplete information. The LocalAgreement algorithm and other streaming policies trade quality for latency.
workaround: Use offline ASR when latency is not critical. For streaming, tune the latency/quality tradeoff parameters (look-ahead window, chunk size) and accept the quality gap.
notes: This is a fundamental tradeoff, not a bug. The Whisper-Streaming paper (arXiv 2307.14743) reports 3.3 seconds latency on unsegmented long-form speech but does not claim parity with offline Whisper. The quality gap is most pronounced at word boundaries and in noisy conditions.
